wagga-wagga-botanic-gardens.name: Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens
wagga-wagga-botanic-gardens.bio: Gardens from 1961 with a rainforest gully, succulent garden, free zoo and aviary, and a miniature railway.
wagga-wagga-botanic-gardens.hours: Open daily (zoo and aviary Thursday to Monday 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM)
notes: ticketUrl omitted: the council pages (wagga.nsw.gov.au) are blocked to scripts; load in a real browser and add the gardens page.
Zoo and aviary days and times (Thu-Mon 9-4, closed Christmas Day and Good Friday) come from a search summary of the blocked council page, not read on the page. Garden opening times not found.
Railway running days not verified, so the bio only says the railway exists (Science Week listing).
No wiki field: name equals the research wiki_title. Pin HIGH (OSM park spelled 'Botanical Garden & Zoo' plus Wikipedia, 51 m); resolve-pin picked the wrong feature and was rejected.

wiradjuri-walking-track.name: Wiradjuri Walking Track
wiradjuri-walking-track.bio: About 42 km of track circling much of Wagga Wagga, with river, hilltop and city views.
notes: Pin is on the track near the riverside start, NOT a computed midpoint: OSM has no single route for the loop (named ways total about 26 km). Replace from the council route map if wanted.
No ticketUrl: council pages are blocked to scripts and no other official page was loaded. The 42 km figure is from Visit NSW.
A popular return route runs from the Visitor Information Centre past Riverside, the Cadell Place murals, Wiradjuri Reserve and Marrambidya Wetland (Visit NSW); left out of the bio for length.

murray-art-museum-albury.name: Murray Art Museum Albury
murray-art-museum-albury.bio: Free regional art museum in Albury, open seven days a week and 362 days a year.
murray-art-museum-albury.hours: Mon–Fri 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM; Sat–Sun and public holidays 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM
notes: Operator page loaded. Closed Anzac Day, Christmas Day and Good Friday (not entered as specialClosures: Good Friday moves).
'Regional' is descriptive wording; the sources do not use it. Pin HIGH.

hume-dam.name: Hume Dam
hume-dam.bio: Dam wall at Lake Hume, built 1919–1936, with a sealed 3.9 km return walk and viewing platforms.
hume-dam.hours: Daylight hours (dam wall access restricted on some days)
notes: ticketUrl omitted: WaterNSW pages are blocked to scripts; open https://www.waternsw.com.au/supply/visit/hume-dam in a real browser and read the current wall-access notice.
Hours and the closure days (wall closed Monday to Thursday for maintenance at one point) are from a search summary of the blocked page; free is inferred, no charge found.
Walk length and build dates are from walkingmaps.com.au. Pin HIGH (OSM dam 'Hume Weir' plus Wikipedia, 80 m); resolve-pin's camp monument was rejected.

shearoutback.name: ShearOutback
shearoutback.bio: Shearing museum and Australian Shearers' Hall of Fame, with live demonstrations at 10:30 am and 1:00 pm.
shearoutback.hours: Mon–Sat 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM; Sun 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM (shearing demonstrations 10:30 AM and 1:00 PM daily)
notes: A$20 adult (concession 15, child under 12 10, family 45), operator Admissions page. Operator suggests at least an hour for the museum and half an hour for the demonstration.
Public-holiday and Christmas closures not found. Pin MEDIUM (OSM 'Shear Outback Hay Visitor Centre').

hay-gaol.name: Hay Gaol
hay-gaol.bio: 1878 gaol turned museum in 1976, with antique windmills and Australia's oldest known bark canoe.
notes: A$5 adult (child 1) is from an undated Visit NSW listing; Visit Hay does not state a price and the shire directory once said A$4. Approximate.
Hay Shire and Visit NSW call it 'Hay Gaol Museum'; the shorter name is kept. Pin HIGH, 1.55 km from the placement point.

dunera-museum.name: Dunera Museum
dunera-museum.bio: Railway-station museum on the 1,984 Dunera Boys and thousands of internees held at Hay in 1940–46.
notes: A$5 entry confirmed by Visit Hay, the Dunera Association and the shire directory. Hours differ: Visit Hay 9-5, the Association and directory 9-6; 9-5 recorded.
A Hay Shire URL slug reads 'closed for restoration' but redirects to the directory home and the current Visit Hay page shows it open; no dated closure found. Guided tours by appointment.
Pin HIGH (OSM Hay Railway Station, where the museum is, plus Commons median).

griffith-pioneer-park-museum.name: Griffith Pioneer Park Museum
griffith-pioneer-park-museum.bio: Council museum telling how the Murrumbidgee Irrigation Area shaped Griffith, open seven days.
griffith-pioneer-park-museum.hours: Mon–Fri 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM; Sat–Sun 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM
notes: A$15 adult (concession 12, child 5-17 8, family 45); Griffith residents free in 2026. Pioneer Express train tour is priced separately.
Christmas and public-holiday closures not read. Pin MEDIUM (OSM museum, 31 m).

cocoparra-national-park.name: Cocoparra National Park
cocoparra-national-park.bio: Range park about 25 km north-east of Griffith, with ridge walks and waterfalls after rain.
cocoparra-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours (NPWS lists 7am to 7pm; closes for weather or fire danger)
notes: Free: no entry fee on the NPWS page (camping at Woolshed Flat is charged). Inferred; confirm.

Pin is the OSM 'Gorge lookout' near Jacks Creek Picnic Area, a central visitor point (MEDIUM). Other visitor areas: Woolshed Falls and Woolshed Flat (-34.081,146.221) and Mount Brogden (-34.205,146.286).
NPWS shows both '7am to 7pm' and 'always open'; unclear which is the gate rule.

junee-roundhouse-museum.name: Junee Roundhouse Museum
junee-roundhouse-museum.bio: Rare working roundhouse opened in 1947, half museum and half workshop for locomotives and rolling stock.
notes: A$15 adult (concession 10, family 35). Open most NSW public holidays; closed Christmas Day, Boxing Day and Good Friday; opens at noon on Anzac Day.
wiki 'Junee Roundhouse' is the research's wiki_title but the research did not record fetching the article; confirm before applying.
Operator calls it one of few working roundhouses in the Southern Hemisphere; bio says 'rare'. Pin MEDIUM.

junee-licorice-and-chocolate-factory.name: Junee Licorice and Chocolate Factory
junee-licorice-and-chocolate-factory.bio: Sweets factory in Junee's old flour mill, with a shop, the Millroom restaurant and self-guided viewing.
junee-licorice-and-chocolate-factory.hours: Open daily 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM (closed Anzac Day)
notes: FLAGGED: guided tours are 'currently unavailable due to renovations'. Written as a free visit (self-guided look at the manufacturing areas 9-4 daily). When tours run they cost A$5 adult, A$4 senior, A$3 child (under 5 free).
Hands-on chocolate making is A$7 per plate (drop-in 9-3). Whether non-customers can enter the production areas free is not stated ('customers are welcome'). Tour resume date unknown.
Use the new domain juneelicoriceandchocolate.com (the old Wix domain errors). Demote to review if the owner wants a tour-based spot. Pin MEDIUM.

bethungra-spiral.name: Bethungra Spiral
bethungra-spiral.bio: Australia's only 360-degree rail spiral, built in the 1940s, seen from a viewing platform above the tunnel.
notes: ticketUrl omitted: only a Junee tourism page exists (youmeandjunee.com.au, a candidate, not the steward).
Free and open access are inferred; the page gives no hours or fee. Pin is the OSM viewing platform, 395 m from the Wikipedia spiral point (MEDIUM).
wiki equals the name, so it is not needed if that is the article title.

dog-on-the-tuckerbox.name: Dog on the Tuckerbox
dog-on-the-tuckerbox.bio: Monument from 1932, 8 km north of Gundagai just off the Hume Highway, based on an 1850s bullocky poem.
dog-on-the-tuckerbox.hours: Open 24 hours (kiosk and farm shop open daily)
notes: The page says the monument was unveiled 28 November 1932 and the legend began with the 1850s poem 'Bullocky Bill'. 24-hour access is inferred (outdoor monument); kiosk hours not verified.
Pin HIGH (OSM attraction, Wikipedia and Commons within 100 m).

rusconis-marble-cathedral.name: Rusconi's Marble Masterpiece
rusconis-marble-cathedral.bio: Miniature cathedral hand-built from more than 20,000 pieces of marble over nearly 30 years from 1910.
rusconis-marble-cathedral.hours: Mon–Fri 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM (closed 12:30–1:00 PM); Sat–Sun 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM
notes: Official name is 'Rusconi's Marble Masterpiece'; id keeps 'rusconis-marble-cathedral'.

On display inside the Gundagai Visitor Information Centre, Sheridan Street; hours are the centre's, which may be reduced or closed on public holidays. A$5 adult (pensioner 3, child 2, family 10); undated page, so unclear if still current after the 2025 centre renovation.
Pin MEDIUM (the visitor centre; no OSM feature for the exhibit).

junction-park-wentworth.name: Junction Park
junction-park-wentworth.bio: Park with a 35-step tower over where the Darling and Murray meet, their waters showing different colours.
notes: ticketUrl omitted: only a Wentworth Shire tourism page (a candidate) exists, with no hours or price. Open access is assumed.
Tower opened 1991 (Rotary Club project). A newer Junction Island viewing platform (Nov 2025) is from a search summary and was not verified. Pin HIGH (OSM park).

old-wentworth-gaol.name: Old Wentworth Gaol
old-wentworth-gaol.bio: Gaol built 1879–81 from bricks made on site, open for self-guided visits; it closed in 1927.
old-wentworth-gaol.hours: Mon–Wed 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM; Sat–Sun 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM
notes: WEAK, UNVERIFIED: hours are from a search summary of a Visit Mildura listing (also closed Christmas Day, Boxing Day, Good Friday); A$8 adult is from one visitor-review aggregator. Confirm with Wentworth Visitor Information Centre (+61 3 5027 5080). closedDays not set (inferred Thu-Fri).
Designed by James Barnett, the first Australian-designed gaol (Wentworth shire page). Shire page heading names the gaol but has no hours or price. Pin MEDIUM.

perry-sandhills.name: Perry Sandhills
perry-sandhills.bio: 160 ha of shifting dunes 6 km west of Wentworth, where a 500-year-old red gum is buried to its canopy.
notes: ticketUrl omitted: only a shire tourism page (a candidate). Access is assumed free and open; land tenure and permit rules are unverified (the dunes host ticketed events).
The red gum is called the God Tree (shire page). Pin HIGH (OSM attraction plus Commons median).

woomargama-national-park.name: Woomargama National Park
woomargama-national-park.bio: Largest protected area of forest west of the Great Dividing Range, with campgrounds and Norths Lookout.
woomargama-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours (NPWS lists 7am to 7pm; closes for weather or fire danger)
notes: Free: no entry fee on the NPWS page (camping charged). Inferred; confirm.

Pin is the OSM viewpoint 'Norths Lookout' on the Tin Mines Fire Trail (MEDIUM); no entrance point found. The Hume and Hovell walking track crosses the park. About 20 km from Holbrook and 30 km from Albury (Wikipedia).

murray-valley-national-park.name: Murray Valley National Park
murray-valley-national-park.bio: River red gum forest in the Riverina's Ramsar-listed wetlands, for kayaking, fishing and birdwatching.
murray-valley-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours (NPWS lists 7am to 7pm; closes for weather or fire danger)
notes: Free: no entry fee on the NPWS page (camping charged). Inferred; confirm.
Pin is the OSM Reed Beds Bird Hide at Mathoura (MEDIUM), one visitor point of a park that is several separate blocks.
NPWS publishes daily river reports.

willandra-national-park.name: Willandra National Park
willandra-national-park.bio: Wetlands and grassy plains with over 195 bird species, including the endangered plains-wanderer.
willandra-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours (NPWS lists 7am to 7pm; closes for weather or fire danger)
notes: A$8 is per vehicle per day, self-registration, bring correct change (NPWS), not per person. This is the only park in the region with a listed entry fee.
Pin is the visitor precinct near the Willandra wool shed and campground (MEDIUM); the old Hillston-side point was 48 km away. Not the same place as Willandra Lakes (Mungo).
The pastoral history (shearing at 'Big Willandra' in the bush song 'Flash Jack from Gundagai') is left out of the bio for length.

yanga-national-park.name: Yanga National Park
yanga-national-park.bio: Murrumbidgee park near Balranald with a red gum bird hide on Yanga Lake and an old homestead and woolshed.
yanga-national-park.hours: Sunrise to sunset (Yanga Homestead precinct 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM)
notes: Free: no entry fee on the NPWS page (camping charged). Inferred; confirm. Cook's Cottage and the refrigeration shed exhibitions open daily.
Up to 150 bird species at the bird hide (NPWS). Pin is the Yanga Homestead precinct, the visitor hub (MEDIUM).

murrumbidgee-valley-national-park.name: Murrumbidgee Valley National Park
murrumbidgee-valley-national-park.bio: Linear Murrumbidgee park protecting part of the world's largest continuous tract of river red gum forest.
murrumbidgee-valley-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours (NPWS lists 7am to 7pm; closes for weather or fire danger)
notes: PIN LOW: any single point on a park running Narrandera to Balranald is arbitrary. This is the NPWS coordinate for the Turkey Flat picnic area and bird hide, near Leeton, which NPWS calls a must-see. Alternative: Sandy Beach (-34.7243,146.4664, OSM beach). Owner to confirm.
Free: no entry fee on the NPWS page (camping charged). Inferred; confirm. Middle Beach is part of this park and stays rejected as its own spot.

the-rock.name: The Rock
the-rock.bio: Grade 3 walk, 6 km return, climbing The Rock formation in Kengal Aboriginal Place to a lookout.
the-rock.hours: Open 24 hours (NPWS lists 7am to 7pm; closes for weather or fire danger)
notes: Pin is the computed midpoint of the surveyed OSM Yerong Walking Track (3.0 km one way, car park -35.2614,147.0761 to lookout -35.2747,147.0742). Use the lookout if a summit pin is preferred.
Free: no entry fee on the NPWS page. The reserve's full name is The Rock Nature Reserve - Kengal Aboriginal Place; shown name kept as 'The Rock'. Bio avoids repeating 'Yerong' to stay short.

holbrook-submarine-museum.name: Holbrook Submarine Museum
holbrook-submarine-museum.bio: Holbrook's submarine museum, run by its Friends group and combined with the Greater Hume visitor centre.
holbrook-submarine-museum.hours: Mon–Fri 9:30 AM – 4:30 PM; Sat–Sun 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM (Apr–Sep) or 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (Oct–Mar)
notes: WEAK BIO: the research page says nothing about the exhibits (no submarine, HMAS Otway or collection facts), so the bio states only what was sourced. Add one distinctive fact once researched.

A$10 adult (family 20, students 5). Entry closes 30 minutes before the visitor centre closes; open public holidays on Monday. Christmas and Good Friday closures not stated. Older aggregators give A$7 and different hours.
No Wikipedia article titled 'Holbrook Submarine Museum' (404), so no wiki. Pin HIGH.

narrandera-flora-and-fauna-reserve.name: Narrandera Flora and Fauna Reserve
narrandera-flora-and-fauna-reserve.bio: River red gum reserve with a colony of over 300 wild koalas, a few minutes' walk from Narrandera.
narrandera-flora-and-fauna-reserve.hours: Daylight hours (access roads closed in wet weather)
notes: Free entry per the NSW Government listing. 'Daylight hours' is an assumption: no opening hours were found. Council closes the unsealed access roads during and after wet weather.
Koalas descend from about 20 reintroduced in the 1970s. Pin HIGH (reserve entrance and car park). Address reads Oakbank Drive or Oakbank Street depending on source.

big-guitar-narrandera.name: Big Playable Guitar
big-guitar-narrandera.bio: 5.82 m plywood guitar built in 1988 by a local, displayed in Narrandera's visitor centre.
big-guitar-narrandera.hours: Mon–Fri 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM; Sat 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM; Sun 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM
notes: Renamed from 'Big Guitar' to the official 'Big Playable Guitar'; id kept. Owner to confirm the shown name.
Hours are the Narrandera Destination and Discovery Hub's; public-holiday hours not read. Pin MEDIUM (the visitor centre, where the guitar is); resolve-pin returned Big Arrow and was rejected.

fivebough-and-tuckerbil-wetlands.name: Fivebough Wetlands
fivebough-and-tuckerbil-wetlands.bio: Ramsar-listed wetlands near Leeton with walking and cycling tracks, viewing shelters and a picnic area.
notes: Renamed from 'Fivebough and Tuckerbil Wetlands': Tuckerbil (283 ha) has no public access, so only Fivebough is the spot. Id kept.

Free per the NSW Government listing. Hours not stated; an older reserve page said a gate key came from the Leeton Visitor Information Centre with a A$10 deposit and vehicles were not permitted. Current rules unverified.
Pin is the OSM reserve centroid (MEDIUM); the entrance is on Petersham Road and was not separately resolved.

tumbarumba-rosewood-rail-trail.name: Tumbarumba to Rosewood Rail Trail
tumbarumba-rosewood-rail-trail.bio: 21 km sealed rail trail through farmland west of the Snowy Mountains, with four station sites and displays.
notes: Opened April 2020 (Visit Snowy Valleys). Pin is the midpoint along OSM route relation 12568572, accurate to about 1-2 km because of small gaps in the geometry (MEDIUM). OSM geometry is about 24 km against the published 21 km.
Free and always open: volunteer site says 'Always open'; no charge found.

bradmans-birthplace-museum.name: Bradman's Birthplace Museum
bradmans-birthplace-museum.bio: Cottage where Donald Bradman was born in 1908, open to the public since 1992, with memorabilia next door.
bradmans-birthplace-museum.hours: Open daily 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (10:00 AM – 4:00 PM June–August)
notes: A$5 adult, children under 16 free. Closed Christmas Day and Good Friday (not entered as specialClosures).
Memorabilia Cottage is at 87 Adams Street (Visit Cootamundra). Pin HIGH.

cricket-captains-walk.name: Cricket Captains Walk
cricket-captains-walk.bio: A 150 m path of bronze busts of Australia's men's Test captains, opened in 1998 with a Bradman sculpture.
notes: The page says Stage 1 opened 30 August 1998 with a life-size Bradman sculpture; the walk is wheelchair accessible. No hours stated; open access assumed.
wiki 'Cricket Captains' Walk' is the research's wiki_title, not confirmed as fetched; check before applying. Pin HIGH (OSM footway midpoint plus Commons).

coolamon-fire-museum.name: Coolamon Fire Museum
coolamon-fire-museum.bio: Old fire station holding firefighting memorabilia from around the world, including 100-plus helmets.
notes: Free, donations welcome; also the Visitor Information Centre. Opened 5 October 2015; helmets date from the 1830s and breathing apparatus from the 1800s. The page is undated; Christmas closures not stated.
Pin HIGH.

temora-aviation-museum.name: Temora Aviation Museum
temora-aviation-museum.bio: Historic ex-military aircraft on the site of the WWII No. 10 Elementary Flying Training School.
notes: A$25 adult (over 65 20, child 3-16 10, family 60). Closed Good Friday, New Year's Day, Christmas Day and Boxing Day (not entered as specialClosures).
Flying-day pricing is separate and not recorded. Pin HIGH.

greens-gunyah-museum.name: Greens Gunyah Museum
greens-gunyah-museum.bio: Lockhart museum with 1888 Shearers' Strike artefacts from Brookong Station and a gallery of wool art.
notes: A$10 adult (secondary 5, primary 1), matched by the 2026 NSW Government listing. The museum site footer reads 2020, so hours may have changed; older directories gave 9:30-4:30 on some days.
The museum's own spelling is 'Green's Gunyah'; research name kept. Pin MEDIUM.

tocumwal-town-beach.name: Tocumwal Town Beach
tocumwal-town-beach.bio: Big Murray River beach in red gum forest near town; unpatrolled, and the current can be treacherous.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach; the only council page covers the whole town. Free is inferred (a search summary only). The beach closes in floods; a primitive camping area is attached (Wikivoyage).
Tocumwal has 25 river beach sites (Berrigan Shire Council). Pin MEDIUM (OSM natural=beach).

big-cod-tocumwal.name: Big Cod
big-cod-tocumwal.bio: Giant fibreglass Murray cod on the Tocumwal foreshore, dated to 1968 and one of Australia's Big Things.
notes: No ticketUrl: roadside sculpture; the only council page is the whole-town page. The 1968 date and 'second oldest' claim are Wikivoyage's, so the bio says 'dated to'. Pin HIGH.

coleambally-bucyrus-dragline.name: Coleambally Bucyrus Dragline
coleambally-bucyrus-dragline.bio: Bucyrus-Erie dragline at the town entrance, the machine that built Coleambally's irrigation system.
notes: Stands in Lions Park; free access is inferred (open park). The council page says the town would not exist without the dragline.
Pin is the Commons median of 16 geotagged dragline files, 114 m from the OSM park (MEDIUM).

biggest-football-ungarie.name: Biggest Football
biggest-football-ungarie.bio: 800 kg fibreglass Sherrin on a five-metre pedestal in Ungarie, a tribute to the Daniher brothers.
notes: Bland Shire calls it 'The Big Football'; research name kept, owner to confirm. In Bing Wallder Park, unveiled March 2018. Free access inferred (public park).
Pin HIGH (OSM artwork plus Commons median 95 m).

held.name: Prince Alfred Bridge
held.reason: Demoted to review: the bridge was demolished in November 2021. Only a memorial concept and the remaining Railway Bridge views exist, and the pin is LOW (Wikipedia point, 69 Commons files).
held.facts: Visit NSW: Prince Alfred Bridge demolished November 2021; the Timber Railway Bridge and twin Sheahan Bridges remain, timber viaducts National Trust listed. Crown Lands released a memorial concept (viewing area off Sheridan Street with a wire sculpture and AR information panel; second site at O.I. Bell Drive; feedback to 31 May); whether it was built is unknown. If wanted, replace it with a Gundagai historic railway bridge / Prince Alfred Bridge memorial viewing-area spot named from https://www.visitnsw.com/destinations/country-nsw/riverina/gundagai/attractions/gundagai-historic-railway-bridge-prince-alfred-bridge-memorial. Pin if kept: -35.0744, 148.1069 (LOW). Category historic, free, Australia/Sydney, no ticketUrl.

held.name: Coleambally Wineglass Water Tower
held.reason: Held for review per the brief. It has no entry in research.json (no facts, hours, cost, source or pin), so no spot can be written from the research.
held.facts: None in research.json. Would need a counted source, a verified pin and confirmation it is a visitor stop, not a roadside look from the pavement. Coleambally already has the Bucyrus Dragline spot; if kept it should not repeat that spot's wording.

notes: 37 spots written plus 2 held (Prince Alfred Bridge, Coleambally Wineglass Water Tower). All are standalone, keyed by the research.json fallback ids, country Australia (AU), continent Oceania, timezone Australia/Sydney. Add the four standalone fields when applying.

No shell was available in this session, so bio-fit.py was NOT run. Bios were counted by hand at roughly 78-112 characters; the tightest are Dog on the Tuckerbox, Junee Roundhouse Museum, Hume Dam, Bradman's Birthplace Museum, Cricket Captains Walk and Dunera Museum. Run `python3 scripts/curation/bio-fit.py` before applying and trim any that wrap past three lines.

Coordinates are the research's coordinates_check.source_point values, copied exactly. LOW or weak pins to confirm: Murrumbidgee Valley National Park (arbitrary point on a linear park), Wiradjuri Walking Track (on-track, not a midpoint). Landmark/institution pins MEDIUM or HIGH otherwise.

ticketUrl omitted (no BLOCKED strings or *_candidate used): Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens, Hume Dam (blocked council and WaterNSW pages), plus Wiradjuri Walking Track, Bethungra Spiral, Junction Park, Perry Sandhills, Tocumwal Town Beach and Big Cod (no steward page).

Parks other than Willandra are free: NPWS lists no entry fee on those pages (inferred; camping and tours are charged). Willandra is A$8 per vehicle per day. NPWS hours show both '7am to 7pm' and 'always open'.

Renames for the owner to confirm: Rusconi's Marble Masterpiece (id kept), Big Playable Guitar, Fivebough Wetlands (Tuckerbil has no public access). Kept as research names though sources differ: Greens Gunyah Museum, Biggest Football, The Rock.
